title: Thermal Resistance Network Derivative (TREND) Model for Efficient Thermal Simulation and Design of ICs and Packages
problem: Conventional thermal simulation of 3-D ICs and packages requires extensive computational resources, causing thermal design timelines to span multiple weeks.
motivation: Accelerating thermal design from weeks to minutes directly reduces IC development cycles and enables faster exploration of thermal-aware design tradeoffs.
method: The TREND model uses thermal resistance network derivatives to dynamically focus the solution domain on thermally critical regions, reducing computational overhead while maintaining accuracy. The approach abstracts non-critical regions while preserving fine-grained detail where it matters most for design validation.
key_novelty: Thermal resistance network derivatives enable selective refinement of simulation domains to prioritize critical thermal regions, achieving massive speedup without sacrificing fidelity.
contributions: TREND model for accelerated thermal simulation of 3-D ICs and packages
2695x speedup over commercial thermal simulation software with accuracy preservation
Modular thermal design capability through internal detail protection
Reduction of thermal design timeline from weeks to minutes
limitations: Paper does not discuss limitations of the thermal resistance network approximation or scalability boundaries.
primary_theme: Efficient thermal simulation for IC design
